I've looked through the source code of Voat and it does require quite a bit of cleaning up for it to be a platform that can be extended and maintained. There's a few really big warning signs on the code, and one of them is that the "front-side" (controllers) of the backend are not decoupled from the business logic, meaning that there will be serious code-duplication which will lead to impossible maintainability which again will stagnate the release schedules. The other part is the atrocious error handling where it seems like the code is written by a person who thinks that the point of exception handling is to prevent the application from crashing (it is not. If there's a programming error, there's a programming error and that needs to be caught and fixed - not shoved under the rug).

But I'm being negative here, which is something best left for reddit :P I feel that Voat is overall much better and cleaner, plus that it feels a lot more "modern" than reddit. It also feels great to start over with a much friendlier crowd. And now that it's gotten a bit more stable from the initial overload, it also feels a lot faster and snappier.

Shit, maybe they need some employees? :P Hopefully it won't limit us to bad from what we want to do.

I'm with you though, I hope we have a smaller, awesome community here vs reddit. Not that I want a place that has no objectivity, but just not a community full of kneejerk reactionists. :P

Well, it's open source so I guess they hope that people might fix it for them (which is unlikely).. All they need to do is take a week to clean up the code, and make it more modular, and remove all the try { ... } catch (Exception) { ... } and replace it with something that actually handles exceptions they anticipate, rather pretending that it "fixes" programming errors. It's not actually that much of a job to do, but it needs to be done sooner rather than later. The larger the code-base is, the harder it will be to do something about, due to inter-code dependencies; meaning code that depends on the current architecture and therefore basically makes the old code forever unchangeable.

I like objectivity, I just don't like people acting like their own personal anxiety is something that requires attention from CIG. If there's some objective reasons for concern, then fine. If it's just whining just because some people are loaded with impatience and emotional instability, then that's not fine :P I've read a lot of people arguing over things they know very little about which is incredibly annoying, like the whole 64-bit farse and people saying that CIG should write their own game engine from scratch. That's also something that should be unacceptable, because it creates uneasiness in the community based on hearsay and conjecture.

So, yes, objectivity definitely. If there was any real cause for concern that doesn't turn out to be based in peoples personal insecurity, that would be something I would embrace. But it always turns out to be a kneejerk reaction as you said.

I look forward to see how this subverse turns out, and I dearly hope that people can make sure that the community stays positive in the anticipation of what could turn out the be the best game in gaming history.

I bought this 1864 Anglican church in a small community in Quebec about an hour north of Ottawa. I have the original 1864 bill of sales when the original land owner sold the lot to the Archbishop of Montreal for 1$.

The bottom will become my metal fabrication shop with a laundry/mechanical room in the back, the top floor will be my loft. I'll put in a few sun wells on the eastern roof slope and add a dormer to the western roof with a patio door opening up to my futur deck overlooking the village and the river.

I'll do an open concept loft with 8' walls separating only the bedroom & washroom from the rest of the 2nd floor.

Lots of stuff was left behind, like my soon to be refurbished GE wringer washer, also a very nice forced air wood burning furnace.

Stay tuned for updates, will post a lot of progress in /v/diy and finished projects here in /v/pics.
